title: Combining, keeping, and how it got here
dek: Part 3 of Git, taken apart. How git combines two histories: merge bases painted with generation numbers, merge-ort's one map and three phases, staged rename detection, conflict styles and rerere. How it keeps a repository fast without locking deletion: auto-maintenance, geometric repacks, prune's two-week clock, the commit-graph and Bloom filters. How a 1,244-line commit from 2005 became v2.55.0, what Git 3.0 will change, and the full register of bugs, documentation drift and gotchas found while reading.
byline: 23 October 2026 · Subject: git@e9019fca (v2.55.0) · Part 3 of 3 · Read from the source and the manual; measured on this machine
description: Git v2.55.0 taken apart, part 3: merge bases and generation numbers, merge-ort, rename detection, conflict styles and rerere, auto-maintenance and geometric repack, prune's grace period, the commit-graph and Bloom filters, history to Git 3.0, and a findings register with reproductions.
og_description: Part 3 of a three-part teardown of git v2.55.0: how merge-ort combines histories and what 'in memory' really writes, why rename detection rarely goes quadratic, why your commits now trigger geometric maintenance instead of gc, how prune stays safe with a clock instead of a lock, what the commit-graph and Bloom filters buy on git.git, and a register of three fixed bugs, latent ones and 29 doc drifts, each with a reproduction.
twitter_description: Git v2.55.0, part 3: merging, maintenance, the commit-graph and Bloom filters, history to Git 3.0, and a findings register with reproductions.
badges_callout:
How to read the badges

from the code marks a fact read from git at e9019fca (tag v2.55.0, 29 June 2026), cited as a path and line number from the repository root; the manual pages are cited under Documentation/. measured here marks a number or behaviour observed with git version 2.55.0 on a Linux box with a 2-vCPU cgroup quota (git's sysconf still sees 8 CPUs), mostly on a clone of git.git itself; the scripts live in ~/git-ref/lab/. Timings are medians of three to five runs, and differences under about 30% are noise. reconstruction marks a judgement I drew from those sources rather than read in one place.

This is Part 3 of 3 of Git, taken apart. Part 1 covers the commit and its objects, packs and bitmaps; Part 2 covers the index, refs, durability and the wire protocol. This part assumes both and does not re-explain their formats.
